dataRef.description: Name of the table whose features are the viewpoints.

sampling.description: The directions each viewpoint looks in, around the horizon. Read with the `centroid` strategy only.

azimuthOffsetDeg.description: Angle of the first direction, in degrees counterclockwise from east (0 looks east, 90 north); the others follow every 360 / `directions` degrees. Defaults to 0.

directions.description: Directions sampled around each viewpoint, evenly spaced. Defaults to 1.

pitchDeg.description: Angle of every direction above the horizontal, in degrees: up when positive, down when negative. Defaults to 0.

floors.description: Rows of windows on each facade, spread evenly up the building's height.

strategy.description: Where the viewpoints are: each feature's centroid (the default), looking in the directions `sampling` sets, or `building-windows`: windows along each building's facades, each looking out from the facade and 30 degrees to either side. workspace.description: Workspace of the tables the pass reads and writes.

RenderLayerSpec.description: A table drawn into the frames a render pass samples.

dataRef.description: Name of the table to draw.

id.description: Name given to the layer in the pass. Letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.

objectIdProperty.description: Property that holds the object's id, for `aggregation.type` `objects`.

type.description: How the layer is drawn into the frames. A render pass draws no points.

ScatterPlotSpec.description: A scatterplot of two or more columns.

axis.description: Columns to plot, in axis order. At least two are required.

axisLabels.description: Titles of the plot's axes, in the order of `axis`, in place of the column names: the x and y axes' titles of a scatter plot, a bar chart, a line chart and a heat matrix, each axis's title of parallel coordinates, and a table's column headers. An axis without a title keeps its column's name, and an axis that holds a transform's output, `@transform`, is titled `value`. A run refuses more titles than `axis` has columns, and two titles alike, since a table finds the column to sort by its header. Read by the Autark adapter; the deck.gl adapter ignores it.

categoricalColorMapInterpolator.description: Color scheme of marks colored by categories: a categorical `scheme*` scheme, `schemeObservable10` by default. The categories take the scheme's colors in the order they first appear, or in `colorMapDomain`'s order, and those past the scheme's last color take that one. A sequential or diverging `interpolate*` name is refused. Read by the Autark adapter; the deck.gl adapter ignores it.

color.description: Column whose values color the marks: a scatter plot's points, a bar chart's bars, and the lines of parallel coordinates, which a click on an axis's title colors by that axis instead. When every value is a number, or a string that reads as one, the marks take `colorMapInterpolator`'s scheme; otherwise the values are categories, and take `categoricalColorMapInterpolator`'s. A heat matrix colors its cells by their values, which `@transform` names. Line charts and tables color no mark by value.

colorMapDomain.description: Categories the plot is colored over, in order: the first takes the categorical scheme's first color, and so on. The values are read as categories, numbers too, and a mark whose value is not among them is drawn in the mark color. It cannot be set with `colorMapRange`. Read by the Autark adapter; the deck.gl adapter ignores it.

colorMapInterpolator.description: Color scheme of marks colored by numbers: a sequential or diverging `interpolate*` scheme, `interpolateReds` by default. The scale's low end takes the scheme's first color and its high end its last: the lowest and highest values, unless `colorMapRange` or `normalization` sets them. A categorical `scheme*` name is refused, since categories take `categoricalColorMapInterpolator`. Read by the Autark adapter; the deck.gl adapter ignores it.

colorMapRange.description: Ends of the color scale of numbers, as `[low, high]` with low less than high. The plot is colored over this range instead of its lowest and highest values, so plots and map layers that set the same range color the same value alike. Values that are categories ignore it, as a layer with a categorical scheme does, and it cannot be set with `colorMapDomain`. Read by the Autark adapter; the deck.gl adapter ignores it.

dataRef.description: Name of the table to plot.

highlightColor.description: Color of the selected marks, and of a table's selected rows, as `#rrggbb`: `#5dade2` by default. autk-plot keeps one highlight color for the page, so every plot it draws there takes it: a run refuses two plots that set different ones, and a run whose plots set none gives back autk-plot's. Read by the Autark adapter; the deck.gl adapter ignores it.

id.description: Name of the plot, which a link in `links` uses as its `source`. Unique among the ids of the maps and plots. Without it a plot is known by its `dataRef`, so two plots of one table need ids: a run refuses two plots known by one name.

mapRef.description: `dataRef` of the map layer this plot links its selection to. A shorthand for a link in `links`.

markColor.description: Color of the marks that are neither colored by value nor selected, as `#rrggbb`: `#bfbfbf` by default. autk-plot keeps one mark color for the page, so every plot it draws there takes it: a run refuses two plots that set different ones, and a run whose plots set none gives back autk-plot's. Read by the Autark adapter; the deck.gl adapter ignores it.

normalization.description: How the ends of the color scale of numbers are found: `minMax`, the default, takes the lowest and highest values; `percentile` takes the values at the `lowerPercentile` and `upperPercentile` percentiles, 2 and 98 when it gives neither, else 0 and 100 for the one it leaves out. Categories ignore it. A map layer's `normalization` reads the same way. Read by the Autark adapter; the deck.gl adapter ignores it.

osmElements.description: Plot an OpenStreetMap layer table as one row per OSM element it was built from, each with the element's tags, `osm_type` and `osm_id` (and `building_id` in a buildings table), rather than one row per table row. A table that is not an OSM layer, a surface, and an OSM table an update changed are plotted row by row, as without it. Read by the Autark adapter only.

selectFields.description: Columns whose values name the rows a selection in this plot selects, so an app can link the selection to other tables that hold those columns. Neither adapter reads it: the Autark adapter's `plot:selection` events still report feature ids.

selection.description: Rows selected when the plot is drawn, by their positions among the rows it draws, as `plot:selection` events and `setPlotSelection` name them. The plot draws them in its highlight color (a binned plot, the bins that hold them), and the map layers it is linked to, by `mapRef` or `links`, highlight the same rows, as after `setPlotSelection`. No `plot:selection` event reports it. A run refuses a position past the plot's last row. Read by the Autark adapter; the deck.gl adapter ignores it.

items.description: A row of a table as a view draws it: its position among the rows the view draws, from 0.

tickFormats.description: d3-format specifiers of the tick labels of the plot's axes, `[x, y]`: a scatter plot's x and y axes; a bar or line chart's x axis, for labels that read as numbers, and its y axis; and every axis of numbers of parallel coordinates, which read only the first. Heat matrices and tables ignore it. Without it, `['~s', '~s']`. Read by the Autark adapter; the deck.gl adapter ignores it.

workspace.description: Workspace the table is read from.

TerrainSpec.description: The ground of a map in 3D, raised to the heights a raster band gives. Read by the Autark adapter; the deck.gl adapter ignores it.

band.description: The band of heights, by its id (`band_1`, ...) or its label, as a raster layer's `getFnv` names one. Defaults to the first band. On a raster of several bands, a band that names none of them is refused.

dataRef.description: Name of the raster table whose band gives the ground's height in each of its cells, in the workspace's units, such as a `geotiff` source of an elevation model in meters. It is a table of the map's workspace. A cell without a value lies at height 0.

UpdateSourceSpec.description: Replaces or changes the rows of a table already loaded, with rows given inline: a FeatureCollection for a table with a geometry, an array of objects for a table without one. Read by the Autark adapter only.

geojsonObject.description: The rows of a table with a geometry. autk-db stores their coordinates as they come, so they are in the workspace's CRS, as `AutkGrammar.data` gives a table's features.

idColumn.description: With `update`, the column that matches a given row to the table's rows: a column such as `month`, or a feature property as `properties.<name>`, such as `properties.parcel_id`.

jsonObject.description: The rows of a table without a geometry, such as a CSV or JSON table loaded without `geometryColumns`.

strategy.description: `replace` swaps every row of the table for the given rows. `update` changes the rows whose `idColumn` value a given row has: in a table with a geometry, each takes the given row's geometry and properties, and no row is added; in a table without one, the given rows replace them, and those that match no row are added.

workspace.description: Workspace of the table.

UrbanSpec.description: An Autark grammar specification. It names at least one of `data`, `compute`, `map` or `plot`.

$schema.description: URL of the JSON Schema this specification follows.

compute.description: Compute passes, run in order after the data is loaded.

layout.description: How the host arranges the maps and plots.

links.description: Links between plots and map layers. The engine does not read them; the adapter wires them once the maps and plots exist.

workspaces.description: How workspaces store their tables, one entry per workspace, set before the first source loads. A workspace without an entry keeps autk-db's CRS and grid. Read by the Autark adapter only.

WindowsComputeSpec.description: Buildings' windows as a table of their own: one point a window, placed along each building's facades as a render pass's `building-windows` viewpoints are, at the middle of the window. Each point is a feature whose id is the window's, with `properties` that name its building (`sourceFeatureIndex`, the building's row in `dataRef`), its facade, its floor (`floorIndex`, from 0 at the bottom) and its size. Runs on the CPU. Read by the Autark adapter only.

dataRef.description: Name of the buildings table whose windows the pass places.

floors.description: Rows of windows on each facade, spread evenly up the building's height.

layerType.description: How the map draws the new table. Defaults to `points`.

outputTableName.description: Name of the table that receives the windows. Later passes, maps and plots read it by this name.

workspace.description: Workspace of the tables the pass reads and writes.

WktGeometryColumns.description: Geometry from one column holding WKT text such as `POLYGON((...))`. Read by the Autark adapter only.

coordinateFormat.description: CRS of the geometry, as an EPSG string. Defaults to `'EPSG:4326'`.

WorkspaceName.description: Name of a workspace: an isolated set of tables with its own extent. The first source loaded into a workspace sets its extent and later sources are cut to it, so two areas that must not clip each other go in two workspaces. A table is found by its name inside its workspace, so two workspaces may hold tables of the same name. Entries without a workspace use the default one. Read by the Autark adapter only.

WorkspaceSpec.description: How a workspace stores its tables: the coordinate system they are kept in, and the grid their coordinates are rounded to. Read by the Autark adapter only.

coordinateFormat.description: CRS the workspace stores its tables in, as an EPSG string such as `'EPSG:3857'`. Each source is transformed to it as it loads, its maps draw in its units, and so are the lengths given in workspace units, such as a join's `near.distance`. autk-db's default is `'EPSG:3395'`, World Mercator, in meters.

name.description: The workspace, by the name sources, compute passes, maps and plots give as their `workspace`. Without it, the default workspace.

precisionGrid.description: Grid every stored coordinate is rounded to, in the CRS's units. autk-db's default is `0.01`, a centimeter in World Mercator. A geometry the grid collapses is refused as it loads.
